name: Freedom of the Shires
desc: A scroll tied with a red and white rose, signed by every parish council in England. Entitles you to drive sheep over the bridge and complain about the bins in any town hall.

name: Carved Lovespoon
desc: Whittled from one piece of cherry wood with a dragon, a chain and a ball in a cage. Wales has decided you're family now. There's no appeal.

name: Silver Quaich
desc: A shallow two-handled cup for sharing a dram. Scotland's way of saying you're welcome at any table, and you're buying the next round.

name: Ulster Linen Sash
desc: Woven in Lisburn, embroidered with the names of every town that vouched for you. Northern Ireland doesn't hand these out lightly. It hands them out firmly.

name: Claddagh Brooch
desc: Two hands, a heart and a crown, from a Galway goldsmith. Love, loyalty and friendship, says the card. Also free tea in most of Connacht.

name: Three Legs Badge
desc: The Manx triskelion in enamel. Whichever way you throw it, it stands. The island reckons the same goes for you.

name: Airbridge Wings
desc: A small enamel pair of RAF-style wings, handed over by a movements officer who says you are now the sort of passenger they stop checking. Valid on every overseas flight, nowhere else.
